en.title: Week 3
en.oneLiner: Teach going down, let standing happen on purpose, grow words without testing, and make the floor bed truly safe.
now: 🐆 Fast, smooth crawler
🪜 Stairs: up yes, down not yet
🛝 Slides down alone
🛒 Many push-walker steps
🧍 Stands alone a few seconds (without noticing)
👯 Stands more near other babies
🗣️ baba · mama · yeye 爷爷 · baibai 拜拜
🎵 Loves music & Ditty Bird
🖊️ Hands you the music pen for help
🦷 Tooth #3 coming · likes soft chicken
🧩 Plays more on her own
🛏️ New floor bed in a fenced area

bigThree.title: Standing on purpose + going down feet-first
lines: She already stands alone by accident. Next: noticing it. Say softly “You’re standing.” No big cheer (it startles her down).
Hold out a toy that needs both hands while she’s at the couch, so she lets go on her own.
Stairs, couch, bed: “Turn around. Feet first.” Guide her hips, start with 1 step, you stay below her.
Standing less at home is normal: crawling is just faster right now.

bigThree.title: First words: echo-and-add, don’t test
lines: She says “mama” → you say “Mama! Mama’s here!” Copy her word, add one.
Pause and wait 3–5 sec (“Bye-…”). If she doesn’t fill it, just say it and move on.
Never “Say mama for Grandma!” Saying words on request comes a few months later.
Pen handoff = she’s asking. “Help? Mama helps! Your turn!”

bigThree.title: Safe floor bed + teething foods
lines: Until her 1st birthday: firm, flat, bare. Fitted sheet only. Books move outside the sleep zone.
Check mattress gaps, fence locked and anchored, cords and outlets out of reach.
Sore gums: fridge-cold (not frozen) teether, soft proteins: salmon, egg, tofu, shredded slow-cooked meat, lentils.
Teething doesn’t cause fever ≥100.4°F. A fever means something else.

cards.title: Stranger anxiety
lines: Very common around 8–12 months. It comes and goes for months.
It’s a good sign: she now knows you are her safe base and can tell familiar from new.
Let people warm up: they talk to you first, offer a toy, wait for her to come.
Don’t force holding or hand her over while she’s crying. Stay close; she can watch from your lap.

cards.title: Why a floor bed?
cards.sub: Our choice, not an official rule
lines: It’s a Montessori choice. The AAP doesn’t recommend or review floor beds. Its rule for under 12 months: a firm, flat, bare surface (crib, bassinet or play yard).
Pros: she can get in/out herself, no crib to climb out of and fall from, a calm “yes” space.
Cons: she can roam at night, so the whole fenced area must be baby-proof; gaps against the wall or fence are a risk; some nights she won’t stay put.
Under 12 months: bare, firm, flat. Keep books outside until her birthday, then ask the pediatrician.

cards.title: Fussy after ~3 hours of active play?
lines: Most likely she’s hungry and tired. Busy movers burn a lot. Offer milk or a snack about every 2–3 hours.
Good quick fuel: milk, yogurt, banana, soft egg, cheese, a few soft crackers with something protein.
True low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) is rare in healthy babies who are eating normally.
Red flags, call now: very sleepy or hard to wake, limp, shaky or sweaty, pale or gray, won’t feed, vomiting, far fewer wet diapers, or a seizure (call 911).

cards.title: Slides: alone, not on your lap
lines: Lap rides can catch her foot and break her shin (a documented toddler injury).
She goes down sitting, feet first, on toddler-size slides. You wait at the bottom.
Touch the slide first: sunny metal can burn.

cards.title: Music as a back-and-forth game
lines: Freeze dance: music on → bounce; off → “FREEZE!”
Rhythm copy: tap the pot twice, wait, copy whatever she does.
Sing slowly and pause before the gesture so she can join in. No “Mozart effect” needed.

daily: Stair or couch “Turn around, feet first” practice
One standing invitation (toys on couch, dance, walker mission), never forced
Hands-busy standing + quiet “You’re standing”
Pen-book 5–10 min: help / more / play
One live music game together
Independent play with check-ins
2–3 echo-and-add word moments (no testing)
“Baibai” wave at real goodbyes
Snack or milk every 2–3 hours on busy days
Same bedtime order, books outside the bed
todos: Floor-bed zone: books out, gaps checked, fence secured, cords/outlets/furniture done
Tell every caregiver: no lap rides on slides
Check no sit-in baby walker is used anywhere
Make a family photo book (mama, baba, yeye)
Start her word list (Chinese + English together)
Start 12-month checkup questions (milk switch, iron, dentist, sleep items)

quiz.q: Ride down the slide with her on your lap?
quiz.why: Her foot can catch while your weight pushes forward: a known cause of toddler shin fractures. Let her slide alone, you at the bottom.

quiz.q: “Say mama for Grandma! Say it!”
quiz.why: Words on request come months later. Testing makes many babies go quiet. Echo her words when she says them instead.

quiz.q: Softly say “You’re standing” when she stands alone?
quiz.why: A calm label helps her notice standing. A big cheer startles her and she plops.

quiz.q: Leave a couple of board books in her floor bed?
quiz.why: Until 12 months the sleep space should be bare. Read in a spot outside the sleep zone.

quiz.q: Give a frozen-solid teether?
quiz.why: Frozen-hard can hurt gums. Fridge-cold is right. Also skip numbing gels and amber necklaces.

quiz.q: Teach “turn around, feet first” on the couch?
quiz.why: The same words and move on couch, bed and stairs make going down automatic.

quiz.q: Use a sit-in baby walker (seat on wheels)?
quiz.why: AAP says they’re never safe (falls down stairs, reaching hot things). Her stand-behind push walker is fine.

quiz.q: She says “ba” for bottle. Correct her?
quiz.why: Just say it back warmly: “Bottle! Here’s your bottle.” Hearing it clearly is how she learns.

quiz.q: Hand her to a new friend while she cries?
quiz.why: Stranger wariness is normal. Let her warm up from your lap; the friend can offer a toy.

quiz.q: Offer milk or a snack when she’s fussy after a long busy morning?
quiz.why: Usually it’s low fuel plus tiredness. Feed first, then see.

quiz.q: Blame a 101°F fever on teething?
quiz.why: Teething doesn’t cause a true fever (100.4°F/38°C+). Something else is going on, so call the doctor.

quiz.q: Hold both her hands high and march her around for a long time?
quiz.why: It takes over her balance, so she isn’t practicing her own. Offer one finger or a push walker.

plays.name: Stair school: feet first
plays.how: Bottom step only. “Turn around. Feet first.” Guide her hips, slide feet to the floor. 1 step → 2 → 3. You stay below.

plays.name: Couch/bed slide-off
plays.how: Same words on the couch and her bed edge: “Turn around, feet first.”

plays.name: Toys on the couch
plays.how: Put a basket of balls or the drum on the couch seat so she has to stand to reach.

plays.name: Push-walker delivery
plays.how: Put a ball in the walker: “Take the ball to Daddy!” Clear, flat path, no stairs nearby.

plays.name: Squat-to-pick-up
plays.how: While she holds the couch, put a toy by her feet. She bends and comes back up.

plays.name: Stand-to-stand gap
plays.how: Move two sturdy pieces of furniture half a step apart so she lets go briefly to cross.

plays.name: Pen-book: help / more / play
plays.how: Handoff = “Help!” (sign). Play it, hand back: “Your turn!” Once or twice hand-over-hand on a big picture, then let go.

plays.name: Freeze dance
plays.how: Music on: bounce. Off: “FREEZE!” On: “GO!” Early self-control.

plays.name: Rhythm copy
plays.how: Tap a pot twice (“boom boom”), wait, then copy whatever she does.

plays.name: Gesture songs
plays.how: Itsy Bitsy, Wheels on the Bus, Row Your Boat. Sing slowly, pause before the gesture.

plays.name: Hide-and-find with a move
plays.how: Hide a toy under a cup, then switch it to another cup while she watches. “Where’d it go?”

plays.name: Point-and-name walk
plays.how: Carry her around: “Where’s the light? There it is!” When she points, look and name it.

plays.name: Copy-me games
plays.how: Wipe the table, phone to ear, clap. Let her copy, then copy her back.

plays.name: Peer time side by side
plays.how: Playdate or music class with 1–2 babies. No need to share, just watching and copying.

plays.name: Daytime “night-night” game
plays.how: Lie on her bed together, eyes closed, “shhh”… “Good morning!” Makes the bed feel calm.

plays.name: Echo-and-add
plays.how: “Mama” → “Mama! Mama’s here!” “Baibai” → “Baibai! Bye-bye, car!”

plays.name: Baibai door game
plays.how: Step out: “Baibai!” + wave, close door, open: “Hi!” Then “Bai…” and pause.

plays.name: Family photo book
plays.how: “Where’s yeye?” Let her pat the picture. Echo any name she says.

plays.name: Hands-busy standing
plays.how: At the couch, offer a big ball or two clappers so she uses both hands and lets go.

plays.name: One step to me
plays.how: Kneel half a step away: “Come to Mama.” A lean counts. Crawling over is fine too.

plays.name: Solo play + check-ins
plays.how: 4–6 toys out, play 2–3 min together, “I’ll be right here,” move a little away. Smile and narrate now and then.

plays.name: Banana or cracker?
plays.how: Hold up two things. Any reach or look is her answer: name it.

steps.do: Calm yourself first: one slow breath, soften your face and voice.

steps.say: Mama used a loud voice. I’m sorry.

steps.do: Reconnect: get low, a hug or touch, eye contact if she wants it.
Hold the limit calmly, with a yes option.
steps.say: Stairs are with Mama. Let’s climb the cushions.

scripts.note: Repair keeps trust strong. She doesn’t need perfect, she needs you to come back.

scripts.when: Going down stairs, couch or bed

steps.do: Guide her hips so her legs go first.

scripts.note: Same words every time. Later she’ll turn herself when she hears them.

scripts.when: She heads for the stairs alone (limit + yes)

steps.do: Move your body between her and the stairs; calm voice.

steps.say: You want to climb! Climb this pillow hill.

scripts.when: She hands me the music pen

steps.do: Do the help sign (flat hand under fist, lift).
Make the music.
Hand the pen back.
Tap fingertips together.

scripts.when: A new person wants to hold her

steps.say: She likes to warm up first. Let’s say hi from here.
steps.do: Keep her on your lap.
Ask them to talk to you, then offer her a toy.

steps.say: Want to show Auntie your ball?
steps.do: Let her decide. No forcing.

scripts.when: Someone offers to ride the slide with her

steps.say: Thanks! We let her go down by herself. Lap rides can hurt little legs.
Can you catch her at the bottom?

scripts.when: She crawls out of bed at night

steps.do: Calm, quiet, dim. Little talk, no play.
If she climbs in herself, whisper:
Wave together.

steps.say: You’re sad. You loved the slide. We’ll come back.
steps.do: Name the feeling, carry her warmly.

timeline.hint: Each step can take days or weeks. She may skip around.

steps.label: Standing without noticing
steps.note: Lets go while busy, then sits or grabs back. (now)

steps.label: Noticing she’s standing
steps.note: A “whoa” look, stays up a bit longer

steps.label: Standing on purpose
steps.note: Lets go because she wants to; stands from a squat in the open

steps.label: 1–3 steps
steps.note: Between furniture or into your arms, then plop

steps.label: Walking
steps.note: Arms up high, lots of falls (normal!)

ruler.label: When healthy babies first walk alone (WHO):

timeline.footer: Many walk at 12–15 months; 16–18 is still normal. Ask the pediatrician if she isn’t walking alone by ~18 months, or anytime you’re worried.

details.title: Why she stands less at home
lines: Babies pick the fastest, safest way to get places. Crawling is fast and rarely ends in a fall.
Lab studies found babies switch to walking once walking gets them farther and faster than crawling.
Push walker = real practice: weight shift, one-leg balance, step after step.

details.title: Why up is easier than down
lines: Going up, she sees where she’s going. Going down means turning around and feeling backward with her feet.
Down usually comes weeks after up, and it has to be taught. Gate top and bottom at home.

details.title: Standing: more ideas
lines: Barefoot on rug, grass or mat: bare feet grip and feel the floor.
Squat-to-stand: a toy on the floor away from furniture.
If she drops to crawl, let her. Offer again later.

details.title: Words: what counts, two languages
lines: ~4 words (baba, mama, yeye, baibai) is on track or a bit early. Most babies say a first word around 12 months.
A word counts when she uses it for the right person or moment.
Count Chinese + English together. Same idea in both (bye-bye/baibai) counts once.
AAP: two languages don’t cause delays. Each adult uses the language they’re most comfortable in.

details.title: Pen-book plan (step by step)
lines: Celebrate the handoff as a request. Add “more” and “play” words.
Hand-over-hand once or twice, then let her try.
Big pictures first; a sticker on the best spot helps.
Fatten the pen with a foam grip (nothing she can bite off). Show “tip down.”
Fade help: hand-over-hand → guide wrist → just tap the spot.

details.title: Floor-bed safety checklist
lines: Firm, flat mattress, low; fitted sheet only. No adult memory foam or topper.
No gaps against wall or fence. Check corners.
No pillows, blankets, bumpers, stuffed toys, books until 12 months. Sleep sack instead.
Nothing small enough to fit through a toilet-paper tube anywhere in the zone.
Fence locked, anchored, no gaps or climbable bars; check pinch points.
Foam tiles thick and locked (she may chew corners).
Cords, outlets, chargers out of reach. Furniture anchored. Room not hot.
Childproof the room as if the fence weren’t there.

details.title: Bedtime routine
lines: Same order, 20–30 min: dim lights → wash → teeth/gums → pajamas + sleep sack → books outside the bed → same song → bed → same goodnight words.
If she falls asleep on the firm padded floor inside the fence, that’s okay. Move her if you can without fully waking her.
Staying in bed takes weeks to months to learn.

details.title: Teething + food plan
lines: Soft proteins: flaked salmon, soft egg, tofu, shredded slow-cooked meat, lentils/beans mashed, soft meatballs, yogurt, cottage cheese.
Iron focus around 12 months. Pair beans/tofu with vitamin C (berries, tomato, broccoli).
Gums: fridge-cold teether or wet washcloth, gum rub, cool soft foods. Ask about acetaminophen dosing.
Skip: frozen-hard teethers, benzocaine/lidocaine gels, amber necklaces.

details.title: Choking safety
lines: Always seated, upright, watched. No eating while crawling or in the car.
Quarter round foods (grapes, cherry tomatoes). No whole nuts, popcorn, hard raw veg, hot-dog chunks.
Gagging (coughing, red face) is normal learning. Choking (silent, can’t breathe, turning blue) is an emergency. Consider an infant CPR class.

details.title: 12-month checkup: questions to bring
lines: CDC 1-year milestones check
Iron / anemia check
Vaccines due
Fluoride varnish; first dentist visit by age 1
Switching to whole milk (AAP: from 12 months, ~16–24 oz/day, from a cup)
When books/lovey can come back into bed
Anything about walking, hearing or talking

details.title: This week’s reading (2 minutes)
lines: Moving changes thinking. Once babies get around on their own, spatial memory, wariness of heights and checking your face all grow. Mostly correlational, so let her move, keep it safe, stay close.
Music: the “Mozart effect” is a myth. Active, social music (bouncing together, rhythm turns) showed promise in small studies. It’s a great way to connect.
Peers: toddlers copy other kids, even days later. That fits her standing longer near other babies.

watch: Won’t bear weight on her legs, or legs seem stiff or floppy
Loses skills: stops crawling, babbling, or saying words she had
Uses one side much more than the other
By 12 months: no pointing or waving, doesn’t respond to her name, doesn’t look where you point, no back-and-forth babble
By ~16 months: no single words in any language (count both languages)
By ~18 months: not walking alone, or fewer than 3 words besides mama/dada
Fever 100.4°F / 38°C or higher, a sudden limp, or won’t stand on a leg after a fall
Seems not to hear. CDC: don’t wait.

zh.title: 第3周
zh.oneLiner: 这两周就抓四件事：教会她安全地往下爬，让站立从“误打误撞”变成自己想站，说话这块只陪不考，再把地床这一圈彻底弄安全。
now: 🐆 爬得飞快，还特别稳
🪜 楼梯会上，还不会下
🛝 滑梯能自己滑
🛒 推着学步推车能走好多步
🧍 偶尔独站几秒，自己都没察觉
👯 有小朋友在旁边就站得更久
🗣️ 会叫爸爸、妈妈、爷爷，会说拜拜
🎵 一听音乐就来劲，最爱 Ditty Bird
🖊️ 点读笔点不准，就塞给你帮忙
🦷 正在出第3颗牙，最爱软嫩的鸡肉
🧩 自己玩的时间变长了
🛏️ 刚换了地床，外面围了一圈围栏

bigThree.title: 自己站 + 倒着下楼梯
lines: 她其实已经能独站几秒了，只是自己没发现。看到她站着，轻轻说一句“宝宝站着呢”就好。别激动地叫好，一激动她就吓得坐下了。
她扶着沙发站的时候，递个得两只手才能接的玩具，她自然就松手了。
下楼梯、下沙发、下床，都用同一句：“转过来，脚先下。”扶着屁股往下送，先练一级，大人站在她下面护着。
最近在家站得少？别慌。爬得快嘛，她当然先选爬。

bigThree.title: 说话：跟着她说，多加一个词，别考
lines: 她叫“妈妈”，你就接：“妈妈在呢！妈妈在这儿！”学她说的，再顺手多给一个词。
可以留个空让她接，比如“拜——”，等个三五秒。没接也没关系，你笑着说完就行。
别让她“表演”：“快，叫奶奶！叫一个！”听指令开口这件事，还得再等几个月。
她把点读笔塞给你，其实就是在求助。“要妈妈帮忙呀？好，妈妈帮你！到你啦！”

bigThree.title: 地床要安全 + 长牙期吃什么
lines: 一周岁前，睡的地方要硬、平、空，只铺床笠。绘本也先拿出去。
床垫和墙、围栏之间不能有缝；围栏扣牢、固定住；电线、插座都让她够不着。
牙龈疼就给冷藏（别冷冻）的牙胶。蛋白质挑软的：三文鱼、鸡蛋、豆腐、炖到一抿就烂的肉、扁豆。
长牙不会烧到38°C（100.4°F）以上。真烧起来了，那是别的原因。

cards.title: 认生
cards.sub: 见了生人就往你怀里钻？正常的
lines: 8到12个月是认生高峰，时好时坏，会反复好几个月。
这其实是好事：说明她知道妈妈就是她的安全感，也分得清谁熟谁不熟了。
给她时间慢慢熟：让对方先和你聊，再递个玩具，等她自己凑过去。
别硬塞给别人抱，哭着的时候更别递出去。你就在旁边，让她坐你腿上先看着。

cards.title: 为什么选地床？
cards.sub: 我们自己的选择，不是官方推荐
lines: 地床是蒙特梭利那一派的做法。美国儿科学会（AAP）没推荐过，也没专门评估过。它对一岁以下只有一个要求：睡在硬、平、什么都不放的地方（婴儿床、摇篮或游戏床）。
好处：她能自己爬上爬下，不用担心从婴儿床翻出来摔着，围栏里就是她随便动的小天地。
麻烦在哪：半夜醒了能到处爬，所以围栏里每个角落都得做好防护；床垫和墙、围栏之间有缝很危险；有些晚上就是不肯老实待在床上。
一岁前记住三个字：硬、平、空。绘本放外面，过完生日再问问医生能不能放回来。

cards.title: 疯玩了三个钟头就开始闹？
lines: 十有八九是又饿又累。这么能动的娃消耗大，大概每2到3小时补一次奶或小零食。
顶饿又方便的：奶、酸奶、香蕉、软炒蛋、奶酪，或者几块软饼干配点蛋白质。
吃得正常的健康宝宝，真正的低血糖很少见，不用太担心。
有这些情况马上打电话：困得叫不醒、浑身软塌塌、发抖或冒冷汗、脸色发白发灰、不肯喝奶、呕吐、尿布明显没以前湿。抽搐就直接打911。

cards.title: 滑滑梯：让她自己滑，别抱着
lines: 大人抱着一起滑，娃的脚一卡住，大人的重量还在往下冲，很容易小腿骨折。这是有记录的常见伤。
让她坐着、脚朝前，自己滑小朋友尺寸的滑梯，你在底下接着。
滑之前先摸一摸，太阳底下晒过的铁滑梯会烫。

cards.title: 音乐要一起玩，别光放着听
cards.sub: 陪着玩比放背景音乐强
lines: 木头人游戏：音乐一响就扭，一停就喊“定！”
学节奏：你敲两下锅，停下来等她，她怎么敲你就怎么学。
儿歌唱慢点，做动作前停一拍，给她跟上的机会。什么“莫扎特效应”，不用追。

daily: 练一次“转过来，脚先下”（楼梯或沙发都行）
给她一个想站起来的理由：沙发上放玩具、一起跳舞、推车送货，不勉强
双手拿着玩具时站一站，轻声说“宝宝站着呢”
点读书玩5到10分钟：帮忙、还要、响啦
一起玩一次音乐游戏
让她自己玩一会儿，你在旁边时不时回应
跟着她说再加一个词，两三次就够（不考）
每次真告别都挥手说“拜拜”
玩得多的日子，2到3小时补一次奶或零食
睡前流程不变，绘本在床外面读
todos: 地床区收拾好：绘本拿走、查缝隙、围栏固定，电线、插座、家具都处理好
跟所有带娃的人说一声：别抱着她滑滑梯
确认不管在哪儿都不用坐式学步车
这周试一种新的软蛋白质
做本家庭相册（妈妈、爸爸、爷爷）
开个小本记她会说的词，中英文一起记
把一岁体检想问的列出来（换奶、补铁、看牙、床上能放什么）

quiz.q: 抱着她坐你腿上一起滑滑梯？
quiz.why: 脚一卡住，大人的体重还在往下冲，幼儿小腿骨折很多就是这么来的。让她自己滑，你在下面接。

quiz.q: “快，给奶奶叫声妈妈！叫一个嘛！”
quiz.why: 听指令开口还得再等几个月。越催越不开口的娃多的是。她自己说的时候，你接住就好。

quiz.q: 她自己站着时，轻轻说一句“宝宝站着呢”？
quiz.why: 平平静静地说出来，她慢慢就知道“这就是站”。一欢呼，她一激动反而坐下了。

quiz.q: 地床上留两本纸板书陪她睡？
quiz.why: 一岁前睡的地方要空空的，什么都不放。绘本放在床外面读。

quiz.q: 牙胶冻得硬邦邦再给她啃？
quiz.why: 冻太硬会伤牙龈，冷藏的就够了。麻药凝胶、琥珀牙链也都别用。

quiz.q: 在沙发上教她“转过来，脚先下”？
quiz.why: 沙发、床、楼梯都用这一句、这一个动作，练多了就成习惯了。

quiz.q: 用那种带座位、带轮子的学步车？
quiz.why: AAP说这种车怎么都不安全：容易连人带车摔下楼梯，还能够着烫的东西。她那种站在后面推着走的学步推车没问题。

quiz.q: 她要奶瓶时说“ba”，要不要纠正她？
quiz.why: 不用纠正。笑着说一遍对的就行：“奶瓶呀，给你奶瓶。”听多了自然就会了。

quiz.q: 她正哭着，就把她递给新朋友抱？
quiz.why: 认生是正常的。让她在你腿上先观察，朋友可以先递个玩具套套近乎。

quiz.q: 忙了一上午她开始闹，先喂点奶或零食？
quiz.why: 多半是饿了加累了。先喂饱，再看情况。

quiz.q: 烧到38.3°C（101°F），觉得是出牙闹的？
quiz.why: 出牙不会真发烧（38°C/100.4°F以上），肯定有别的原因，打电话问医生。

quiz.q: 长时间拎着她两只手举高“学走路”？
quiz.why: 这样是你在帮她找平衡，她自己的平衡练不到。给她一根手指扶就好，或者让她推学步推车。

plays.name: 楼梯课：倒着下
plays.how: 就用最下面那一级。“转过来，脚先下。”扶着屁股，让脚慢慢滑到地上。一级练熟了再两级、三级，大人始终在下面护着。

plays.name: 从沙发、床上滑下来
plays.how: 沙发边、床边也用同一句：“转过来，脚先下。”

plays.name: 玩具放沙发上
plays.how: 一篮小球或小鼓摆在沙发上，想玩就得站起来够。

plays.name: 推车送快递
plays.how: 球放进学步推车：“把球送给爸爸！”路要清干净、地要平，附近别有楼梯。

plays.name: 蹲下捡玩具
plays.how: 她扶着沙发站时，在脚边放个玩具。弯腰捡起来再站好，腿上就有劲了。

plays.name: 跨小沟
plays.how: 两件稳当的家具拉开半步，她得松一下手才过得去。

plays.name: 点读书：帮忙、还要、响啦
plays.how: 她递笔就说“帮忙！”（配手势），点响了再还给她：“到你啦！”握着她的手点一两次大图，然后放手让她自己来。

plays.name: 木头人跳舞
plays.how: 音乐响就一起扭，音乐停喊“定！”，再响喊“动！”。这是最早的自控力练习。

plays.name: 学节奏
plays.how: 敲两下锅“咚咚”，停下来等她，她怎么敲你就怎么学。

plays.name: 手指谣
plays.how: 《小星星》《两只老虎》《拔萝卜》，边唱边做动作。唱慢点，做动作之前停一拍等等她。

plays.name: 杯子换位藏玩具
plays.how: 玩具扣在一个杯子下，当着她的面挪到另一个杯子下：“咦，跑哪去啦？”

plays.name: 指一指，说一说
plays.how: 抱着她在家里溜达：“灯呢？在那儿！”她一伸手指，你就顺着看过去，告诉她那是什么。

plays.name: 跟我学
plays.how: 擦桌子、拿手机贴耳朵、拍拍手，让她学你，你也学她。

plays.name: 跟小朋友一起玩
plays.how: 约一两个差不多大的宝宝，或者去上音乐课。不用教她分享，在旁边看着学就是在玩。

plays.name: 白天玩“睡觉觉”游戏
plays.how: 一起躺到她床上，闭眼，“嘘——”，再睁眼：“早上好！”让她觉得床是个安心的地方。

plays.name: 跟着说，多一个词
plays.how: 她说“妈妈”，你说“妈妈在这儿！”；她说“拜拜”，你说“拜拜，车车拜拜！”

plays.name: 门口拜拜游戏
plays.how: 一个人出门挥手：“拜拜！”关上门，再打开：“嗨！”之后说“拜——”停一下，等她接。

plays.name: 翻家庭相册
plays.how: “爷爷在哪儿呀？”让她拍拍照片。她叫出谁，你就跟着说一遍。

plays.name: 双手拿着站一站
plays.how: 她扶着沙发站时，递个大球或两个能对敲的玩具。要两只手接，自然就松开沙发了。

plays.name: 走一步扑进妈妈怀里
plays.how: 在她前面半步远跪着张开手：“来，到妈妈这儿。”身子往前一扑也算数，爬过来也没关系。

plays.name: 独立玩 + 时不时回应
plays.how: 摆4到6个玩具，先陪玩两三分钟，说一句“妈妈就在这儿”，再稍微走开点。时不时冲她笑笑，说说她在干嘛。

plays.name: 香蕉还是饼干？
plays.how: 两样东西举起来让她选。伸手也好、看一眼也好，都算她的回答，你帮她说出来。

scripts.when: 我冲她发火了，怎么修复

steps.do: 先稳住自己：深吸一口气，表情和语气都放软。

steps.say: 妈妈刚才太大声了，对不起。

steps.do: 蹲下来抱抱她、摸摸她，她愿意的话看着她的眼睛。
规矩照样守，但给她一个能做的选择。
steps.say: 楼梯要妈妈陪着才能爬。走，我们去爬靠垫山！

scripts.note: 修复关系比不犯错更重要。她要的不是完美妈妈，是一个会回来抱她的妈妈。

steps.do: 扶着她屁股，让腿先往下。

scripts.note: 每次都说同一句。慢慢地，她一听到就会自己转身。

steps.do: 用身体挡在她和楼梯中间，语气平和。

steps.say: 停，楼梯要妈妈陪着才能爬。
想爬是吧？来，爬这个枕头山！

steps.do: 做“帮忙”手势：一只手握拳，放在另一只摊平的手掌上，一起往上抬。
点出声音。
把笔还给她。
两只手的指尖碰一碰。

steps.say: 她得先熟悉一下，咱们先在这儿打个招呼吧。
steps.do: 让她继续坐在你腿上。
请对方先跟你聊几句，再递个玩具给她。

steps.say: 要不要给阿姨看看你的球呀？
steps.do: 过不过去由她，不勉强。

scripts.when: 有人想抱着她一起滑滑梯

steps.say: 谢谢呀！我们让她自己滑，抱着滑容易伤到小腿。
你帮我在下面接着她好吗？

steps.do: 安静、小声、灯调暗。少说话，别陪玩。
她自己爬回去的话，小声夸一句：

steps.say: 再滑两次，我们就上车回家。

steps.do: 一起挥手。

steps.say: 舍不得是不是？你最喜欢滑滑梯了。我们下次再来。
steps.do: 说出她的感受，抱着她温柔地走。

timeline.hint: 每一步可能几天，也可能几周，跳着来也很正常。

steps.label: 站着，自己没察觉
steps.note: 玩得入神时松了手，回过神就坐下或赶紧扶住。（现在）

steps.label: 发现自己站着
steps.note: 会“咦”一下，低头看看或看看你，站得稍微久一点

steps.label: 想站就站
steps.note: 因为想站才松手；没东西扶也能从蹲着站起来

steps.label: 站得越来越久
steps.note: 5秒、10秒，再到20秒以上，手里可能还拿着玩具

steps.label: 迈出1到3步
steps.note: 在家具之间，或者扑进你怀里，然后一屁股坐下

steps.label: 会走了
steps.note: 两手举高找平衡，摔跤是家常便饭（正常！）

ruler.label: 健康宝宝第一次独立走路的月龄（世界卫生组织数据）：

timeline.footer: 多数宝宝12到15个月会走，16到18个月才走也正常。快18个月还不会自己走，或者你心里没底，随时可以问医生。

details.title: 为什么她在家反而站得少
lines: 宝宝想去哪儿，会挑最快最稳的办法。现在爬得又快又不容易摔，当然先爬。
研究发现，等到走比爬去得更远、更快，宝宝才会彻底改成走。
推学步推车就是实打实的练习：重心往前、单脚撑一下、一步接一步。

details.title: 为什么会上不会下
lines: 往上爬，眼睛看得见要去哪儿。往下得先转身，再用脚往后探，难多了。
会下通常比会上晚几周，而且得教，不会自己冒出来。家里楼梯上下都装好护栏。

details.title: 练站立的更多小办法
lines: 光脚站在地毯、草地或爬行垫上，脚底抓得住地，平衡更好。
从蹲到站：玩具放在离家具远一点的地上。
她要是又趴下去爬了，随她。过会儿再给她机会。

details.title: 说话：怎么才算会了一个词？双语怎么算？
lines: 会4个词左右（爸爸、妈妈、爷爷、拜拜）完全在正常范围，甚至还偏早。大多数宝宝一岁前后才冒出第一个词。
只要她是对着对的人、在对的场合说，就算真会了。
中文英文加起来算。同一个意思两种说法（bye-bye和拜拜）只算一个。
AAP说双语不会导致说话晚。家里每个人用自己最顺口的语言跟她聊就好。

details.title: 点读书怎么一步步教
lines: 她递笔就当她在求助，好好回应。再慢慢加上“还要”“响啦”。
握着她的手点一两次，然后放手让她自己试。
先挑图大的页；在最好点的地方贴个贴纸当靶子。
笔身套个泡棉握套，变粗好握（别有能咬下来的小块）。示范给她看“笔尖朝下”。
帮得越来越少：先握着手，再扶手腕，最后只指一下位置。

details.title: 地床安全清单
lines: 床垫硬、平、低，只铺床笠。别用成人记忆棉，也别加褥子。
床垫和墙、围栏之间不能有缝，四个角都要查。
一岁前不放枕头、被子、床围、毛绒玩具和书，用睡袋保暖。
围栏里不能有能塞进卫生纸芯的小东西。
围栏扣牢、固定好，没有缝隙，没有能踩着往上爬的横杆，合页、卡扣处别夹手。
爬行垫要厚、拼紧（她可能会啃边角，小心咬下来的碎块）。
电线、插座、充电器统统够不着；柜子固定在墙上；房间别太热。
整个房间按“没有围栏”的标准来防护，总有一天她会翻出来。

details.title: 睡前流程
lines: 每天一个顺序，20到30分钟：灯调暗 → 洗洗 → 刷牙或擦牙龈 → 换睡衣、穿睡袋 → 在床外读绘本 → 唱同一首歌 → 上床 → 说同一句晚安。
她要是在围栏里那块硬平的垫子上睡着了也没事，能不弄醒就把她挪回床垫。
学会乖乖待在床上，要几周到几个月，急不来。

details.title: 长牙期辅食安排
lines: 软的蛋白质：三文鱼碎、嫩鸡蛋、豆腐、炖烂的肉丝、压碎的豆子或扁豆、软肉丸、酸奶、茅屋奶酪。
一岁前后特别要补铁。吃豆子、豆腐时配点维C高的（莓果、番茄、西兰花），吸收更好。
牙龈疼：冷藏牙胶或冷藏过的湿毛巾、干净的手指揉揉牙龈、凉凉软软的食物。退烧止痛药（对乙酰氨基酚）用量问医生。
别用：冻硬的牙胶、含苯佐卡因或利多卡因的凝胶、琥珀牙链。

details.title: 防噎要点
lines: 吃东西一定坐好、有人盯着。边爬边吃、坐车吃都不行。
圆的食物（葡萄、小番茄）切成四瓣。整颗坚果、爆米花、硬的生蔬菜、热狗块都不给。
干呕（咳、脸红）是在学吃饭，正常。噎住（发不出声、喘不上气、发紫）是急症。有空可以去上一节婴幼儿急救课。

details.title: 一岁体检要问的
lines: CDC一岁发育里程碑
查铁、查贫血
这次要打哪些疫苗
涂氟；一岁前第一次看牙医
换全脂牛奶（AAP：12个月起，每天约470–710毫升，用杯子喝）
什么时候能把绘本、安抚玩偶放回床上
走路、听力、说话方面的任何疑问

details.title: 本周小科普（2分钟）
lines: 会爬会走，脑子也跟着变。宝宝能自己到处移动以后，空间记忆、怕高、看大人脸色判断安不安全，这些能力会一起冒出来。不过多是相关研究，所以：放手让她动，保证安全，你在旁边就好。
音乐：“听莫扎特变聪明”是个误会。真正有点效果的是大人陪着一起玩，一起摇、轮流敲节奏，而且也只是小样本研究。它最大的价值是亲子互动。
小伙伴：小娃会模仿别的小娃，隔几天还记得。难怪她一有小朋友在旁边就站得更久。

watch: 扶着站时腿不肯吃劲，或者腿看着特别僵、特别软
本来会的不会了：不爬了、不咿呀了，或者以前会说的词不说了
满12个月：不会指东西、不会挥手，叫名字没反应，不顺着你指的方向看，也不跟你一来一回地咿咿呀呀
16个月左右：哪种语言都还没有一个词（中英文加起来算）
18个月左右：还不会自己走，或者除了爸爸妈妈不到3个词
发烧38°C / 100.4°F及以上，突然一瘸一拐，或者摔了以后一条腿不肯着地
好像听不见。CDC的建议是：别等，早点问。
